name: Car
title: Car mechanics (1.8 L four-cylinder, 5-speed manual)
intro: This is a front-wheel-drive car. The body is on the outside; explode it (🧩) to see the engine, gearbox, differential, steering and brakes. Tap a part to see what it is, or ask me "How do the pistons turn the wheels?"
suggest: How do the pistons turn the wheels?
Why does the camshaft turn slower than the crankshaft?
What does the differential do in a turn?
looksLike: car, sedan, saloon, SUV, car engine, tyre, brake disc, steering wheel, gearbox

ride.hint: You're in the driver's seat (the body is off, like a convertible). Drag to look around; open the throttle and change gear to see how engine rpm and speed change; tap X-ray to see the engine and gearbox in front of you.

block.name: Engine block
block.info: The main body of the engine, with four cylinders inside. The pistons run up and down in the cylinders, and coolant flows through the water jacket around them.

head.name: Cylinder head
head.info: Sits on top of the block. The combustion chambers, intake and exhaust valves and spark plugs are all here.

valve_cover.name: Valve cover
valve_cover.info: Covers the camshafts and valve gear and keeps the oil in.

oil_pan.name: Oil pan
oil_pan.info: The oil reservoir at the bottom of the engine. Oil is pumped up from here to lubricate the crankshaft, rods and pistons.

crankshaft.name: Crankshaft
crankshaft.info: The engine's main shaft. The four connecting rods sit on offset crank pins, turning the pistons' up-and-down motion into rotation.

crank_pulley.name: Crank pulley
crank_pulley.info: On the front of the crankshaft. It drives the timing belt and the belt for the alternator and air-con compressor.

flywheel.name: Flywheel
flywheel.info: A heavy disc that stores rotational momentum, so the engine runs smoothly while the four cylinders take turns firing. The clutch presses against it.

piston_1.name: Piston 1
piston_1.info: Cylinder 1's piston. Burning gas pushes it down, and the push turns the crankshaft through the connecting rod.

piston_2.name: Piston 2
piston_2.info: Cylinder 2's piston. Burning gas pushes it down, and the push turns the crankshaft through the connecting rod.

piston_3.name: Piston 3
piston_3.info: Cylinder 3's piston. Burning gas pushes it down, and the push turns the crankshaft through the connecting rod.

piston_4.name: Piston 4
piston_4.info: Cylinder 4's piston. Burning gas pushes it down, and the push turns the crankshaft through the connecting rod.

conrod_1.name: Connecting rod 1
conrod_1.info: Links piston 1 to the crankshaft. The top end moves straight up and down with the piston, the bottom end circles with the crank pin, so the rod swings side to side.

conrod_2.name: Connecting rod 2
conrod_2.info: Links piston 2 to the crankshaft. The top end moves straight up and down with the piston, the bottom end circles with the crank pin, so the rod swings side to side.

conrod_3.name: Connecting rod 3
conrod_3.info: Links piston 3 to the crankshaft. The top end moves straight up and down with the piston, the bottom end circles with the crank pin, so the rod swings side to side.

conrod_4.name: Connecting rod 4
conrod_4.info: Links piston 4 to the crankshaft. The top end moves straight up and down with the piston, the bottom end circles with the crank pin, so the rod swings side to side.

camshaft_intake.name: Intake camshaft
camshaft_intake.info: Its cams push the intake valves open in order. It turns at half the crankshaft's speed, because a four-stroke engine takes in air once every two turns.

camshaft_exhaust.name: Exhaust camshaft
camshaft_exhaust.info: Pushes the exhaust valves open in order to let the burnt gas out. It also turns at half the crankshaft's speed.

timing_belt.name: Timing belt
timing_belt.info: A toothed belt that keeps the camshafts at exactly 1:2 with the crankshaft. If it breaks, the valves and pistons can collide.

intake_manifold.name: Intake manifold
intake_manifold.info: Pipes that share the incoming air evenly between the four cylinders.

exhaust_manifold.name: Exhaust manifold
exhaust_manifold.info: Collects the exhaust from the four cylinders into one pipe.

exhaust.name: Exhaust
exhaust.info: The exhaust gas is cleaned by the catalytic converter, quietened by the silencer, and leaves at the back of the car.

radiator.name: Radiator
radiator.info: Coolant that has picked up heat in the engine flows here, is cooled by the oncoming air, and flows back to the engine.

battery.name: Battery
battery.info: A 12-volt battery. It powers the starter motor to start the engine and runs the car's electrics when the engine is off.

gearbox.name: Gearbox
gearbox.info: The case around the gears. With a transverse engine, the gearbox and the differential are built as one unit.

input_shaft.name: Input shaft
input_shaft.info: Turns with the engine when the clutch is engaged; its gears drive the gear wheels on the output shaft.

output_shaft.name: Output shaft
output_shaft.info: Turned by the selected gear, it sends the power on to the differential.

gear_1.name: 1st gear
gear_1.info: 1st gear on the output shaft: the biggest, with the most torque and the least speed. Used to pull away.

gear_2.name: 2nd gear
gear_2.info: 2nd gear on the output shaft: a little smaller than 1st.

gear_3.name: 3rd gear
gear_3.info: 3rd gear on the output shaft: the gear engaged right now (drawn in brass).

gear_4.name: 4th gear
gear_4.info: 4th gear on the output shaft: close to one to one.

gear_5.name: 5th gear
gear_5.info: 5th gear on the output shaft: the smallest. Low rpm and the best fuel economy at speed.

differential.name: Differential
differential.info: The big ring gear (59 teeth) reduces the speed once more; the small gears inside let the outer wheel turn faster than the inner one in a turn.

driveshaft_l.name: Left driveshaft
driveshaft_l.info: Carries power from the differential to the left front wheel. The constant-velocity joints at each end let the wheel move up and down and steer.

driveshaft_r.name: Right driveshaft
driveshaft_r.info: Carries power from the differential to the right front wheel.

knuckle_fl.name: Left steering knuckle
knuckle_fl.info: Holds the left front wheel. It turns about the tilted kingpin axis, and that steers the wheel.

knuckle_fr.name: Right steering knuckle
knuckle_fr.info: Holds the right front wheel. It turns about the tilted kingpin axis, and that steers the wheel.

wheel_fl.name: Left front wheel
wheel_fl.info: The left front wheel. The front wheels drive and steer.

disc_fl.name: Left front brake disc
disc_fl.info: An iron disc that turns with the left front wheel; the caliper squeezes it when you brake.

caliper_fl.name: Left front brake caliper
caliper_fl.info: When you press the brake, hydraulic pressure pushes the caliper's piston and the pads squeeze the left front disc.

wheel_fr.name: Right front wheel
wheel_fr.info: The right front wheel. The front wheels drive and steer.

disc_fr.name: Right front brake disc
disc_fr.info: An iron disc that turns with the right front wheel; the caliper squeezes it when you brake.

caliper_fr.name: Right front brake caliper
caliper_fr.info: When you press the brake, hydraulic pressure pushes the caliper's piston and the pads squeeze the right front disc.

wheel_rl.name: Left rear wheel
wheel_rl.info: The left rear wheel. The rear wheels just roll along; they don't drive.

disc_rl.name: Left rear brake disc
disc_rl.info: An iron disc that turns with the left rear wheel; the caliper squeezes it when you brake.

caliper_rl.name: Left rear brake caliper
caliper_rl.info: When you press the brake, hydraulic pressure pushes the caliper's piston and the pads squeeze the left rear disc.

wheel_rr.name: Right rear wheel
wheel_rr.info: The right rear wheel. The rear wheels just roll along; they don't drive.

disc_rr.name: Right rear brake disc
disc_rr.info: An iron disc that turns with the right rear wheel; the caliper squeezes it when you brake.

caliper_rr.name: Right rear brake caliper
caliper_rr.info: When you press the brake, hydraulic pressure pushes the caliper's piston and the pads squeeze the right rear disc.

strut_fl.name: Left front strut
strut_fl.info: Spring and damper built into one strut (MacPherson type). It holds up the car and soaks up the road.

control_arm_fl.name: Left front lower control arm
control_arm_fl.info: Connects the bottom of the knuckle to the subframe, so the wheel can move up and down but not wander back and forth.

strut_fr.name: Right front strut
strut_fr.info: Spring and damper built into one strut (MacPherson type). It holds up the car and soaks up the road.

control_arm_fr.name: Right front lower control arm
control_arm_fr.info: Connects the bottom of the knuckle to the subframe, so the wheel can move up and down but not wander back and forth.

subframe.name: Subframe
subframe.info: The frame that carries the engine, gearbox and front suspension.

rear_axle.name: Rear axle
rear_axle.info: A torsion-beam rear axle: the left and right rear wheels are joined by a beam that can twist.

spring_rl.name: Left rear spring
spring_rl.info: Holds up the car's weight, compressing and springing back to absorb bumps.

shock_rl.name: Left rear shock absorber
shock_rl.info: Stops the spring from bouncing on: oil inside flows through small holes and turns the bounce into heat.

spring_rr.name: Right rear spring
spring_rr.info: Holds up the car's weight, compressing and springing back to absorb bumps.

shock_rr.name: Right rear shock absorber
shock_rr.info: Stops the spring from bouncing on: oil inside flows through small holes and turns the bounce into heat.

steering_wheel.name: Steering wheel
steering_wheel.info: Turn the wheel and the steering column turns the steering rack's pinion, which pushes the rack to steer the front wheels.

steering_column.name: Steering column
steering_column.info: The shaft from the steering wheel to the steering rack. It has a universal joint and collapses in a crash.

steering_rack.name: Steering rack
steering_rack.info: A small pinion meshes with a toothed rack, turning the wheel's rotation into a side-to-side push that moves the knuckles through the tie rods.

fuel_tank.name: Fuel tank
fuel_tank.info: Sits under the back seat and holds the petrol. A fuel pump sends it to the engine's injectors.

body.name: Body
body.info: The whole outer shell. The steel body is also the car's skeleton: in a crash the front and back crumple first to absorb the force, and the cabin in the middle stays whole. Explode it (🧩) and it lifts off in one piece to show the mechanism inside.

hood.name: Bonnet
hood.info: Covers the engine bay. Its hinges are on the windscreen side, so the front edge lifts when it opens.

door_fl.name: Left front door (driver)
door_fl.info: The hinges are on the door's front edge, so at speed the wind presses the door shut instead of blowing it open. A crash beam inside protects the side.

door_fr.name: Right front door
door_fr.info: The hinges are on the door's front edge, so at speed the wind presses the door shut instead of blowing it open. A crash beam inside protects the side.

door_rl.name: Left rear door
door_rl.info: The hinges are on the door's front edge, so at speed the wind presses the door shut instead of blowing it open. A crash beam inside protects the side.

door_rr.name: Right rear door
door_rr.info: The hinges are on the door's front edge, so at speed the wind presses the door shut instead of blowing it open. A crash beam inside protects the side.

trunk.name: Boot lid
trunk.info: Hinged at the bottom of the rear window; it lifts up to open.

seat_fl.name: Driver's seat
seat_fl.info: This is a left-hand-drive car, so the driver's seat is on the left, facing the steering wheel and pedals.

seat_fr.name: Passenger seat
seat_fr.info: The front seat on the right.

seat_rear.name: Back seat
seat_rear.info: The rear bench, sitting just ahead of the rear axle.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.info: The instruments behind the steering wheel show speed and rpm; the climate controls and audio are in the middle. The steering column and lots of wiring hide underneath.

floor_pan.name: Floor pan and firewall
floor_pan.info: The carpeted cabin floor. The slope at the front is the footwell and the firewall, which separates the engine bay from the cabin; the hump in the middle is the tunnel for the gearbox and exhaust.

pedals.name: Pedals (clutch, brake, accelerator)
pedals.info: In a left-hand-drive manual car, left to right: clutch, brake, accelerator, all hanging from the pedal box under the dashboard. The brake pedal's pushrod goes through the firewall to the brake booster.

brake_booster.name: Brake booster and master cylinder
brake_booster.info: The black drum is the vacuum booster, which uses the engine's vacuum to multiply your foot's force; the master cylinder in front turns that force into hydraulic pressure and sends it down the brake lines to the four calipers. The small see-through tank on top holds the brake fluid.

drives.engine: Engine idling (crankshaft, pistons, camshafts; in neutral)
drives.power: Driving in 3rd (engine → gearbox → differential → front wheels)
drives.steer: Steering left and right (the front wheels follow)
drives.open: Opening the doors, bonnet and boot

steps.say: The fuel-air mixture in the cylinder ignites and expands, pushing the piston down.

quiz.q: When the mixture ignites in the cylinder, the piston is…
options: pushed down
The burning gas expands and pushes the piston down: the only one of the four strokes that produces power.
sucked up
Burning means expansion, not suction; the piston goes back up thanks to the crankshaft's momentum.

steps.say: The connecting rod turns the piston's up-and-down motion into the crankshaft's rotation. Watch the bottom of the rod go round in a circle.

quiz.q: When pistons 1 and 4 are at the top, where are pistons 2 and 3?
options: At the bottom
The crank pins are paired 180° apart: with 1 and 4 up, 2 and 3 are down, which keeps the engine balanced.
Also at the top
Four pistons going up and down together would shake badly, so the crank pins are 180° apart.
Halfway
An inline four's crank pins point only two ways: up or down.

steps.say: Through the timing belt the crankshaft drives the two camshafts at half speed, opening the intake and exhaust valves at the right moment.

quiz.q: The crankshaft turns twice. How many times does the camshaft turn?
options: Once
The four strokes (intake, compression, power, exhaust) take two crank turns, and each valve opens only once in that time.
Twice
Then each valve would open twice and the valve timing would be wrong.
Four times
The camshaft is slower than the crankshaft, not faster.

steps.say: The flywheel stores momentum, and the four cylinders fire in the order 1-3-4-2, so one cylinder works every half turn and the engine runs smoothly.

power.title: How the engine's force reaches the wheels

steps.say: The engine turns the crankshaft and flywheel; with the clutch engaged, the gearbox input shaft turns too.
The input shaft drives the 3rd gear that is engaged now, which turns the output shaft slower but with more force.

quiz.q: A small gear drives a big gear. The big gear turns…
options: slower, with more force
The gear ratio works like a lever: the slower side gets more torque. That's why you pull away in 1st.
faster, with more force
Speed and torque trade against each other; you can't increase both.
as fast as the small gear
Different tooth counts mean different speeds.

steps.say: The differential reduces the speed once more and sends it through the left and right driveshafts to the two front wheels. This car is front-wheel drive.

quiz.q: Which two wheels drive this car?
options: The front wheels
The engine, gearbox and differential are all at the front, and the driveshafts go straight to the front wheels: front-wheel drive.
The rear wheels
There are no driveshafts at the back; the rear wheels just roll along.
All four
Four-wheel drive needs a rear differential and a propshaft, and this car has neither.

steps.say: In a turn the outer wheel travels further, and the small gears in the differential let it turn faster than the inner wheel.

quiz.q: In a turn, which wheel turns faster, the outer or the inner?
options: The outer wheel
The outer arc is bigger, so in the same time it has to cover more distance and turn more.
The inner wheel
The inner arc is smaller, so it covers less distance.
Both the same
Then the tyres would scrub along the ground, which is why there's a differential.

steer.title: How the steering wheel turns the front wheels

steps.say: Turn the steering wheel and the steering column turns with it.
The steering rack's pinion pushes the rack sideways, and the tie rods push the steering knuckles.
The knuckle turns about the kingpin and the front wheel steers. Turn the steering wheel 15° and the wheel turns about 1°.

quiz.q: Turn the steering wheel 180° (half a turn). About how far do the front wheels turn?
options: About 12°
The steering ratio is about 15:1, and 180 ÷ 15 = 12°, so a light touch can turn heavy wheels.
At one to one the steering would be very heavy, and the slightest wobble of your hands would swerve the car.
The wheels can only turn 30-odd degrees at most.

brake.title: From brake pedal to a stop

steps.say: Press the brake pedal and the brake fluid carries the pressure to all four calipers.
The pistons in the calipers push the pads out to squeeze the discs that turn with the wheels.

quiz.q: What do the brake calipers squeeze?
options: The discs that turn with the wheels
The disc is bolted to the wheel, so squeezing it holds the wheel back.
The tyres
Squeezing the tyres would wear them out; the braking surface is the disc.
The driveshafts
There are driveshafts only at the front, and all four wheels need to stop.

steps.say: Friction turns the car's speed into heat. The discs can reach several hundred degrees, which is why they're iron and ventilated.

belt_snap.title: Broken timing belt
belt_snap.short: The crankshaft turns, but the engine won't start
belt_snap.symptom: You turn the key: the crankshaft and pistons move, but the engine just won't start. What do you think is broken?
belt_snap.hint: To start, the valves have to open at the right time. When the crankshaft turns, do the camshafts up top turn with it?
belt_snap.observe: The crankshaft turns. Check whether anything in the top half of the engine moves with it.
whys: With a flat battery the starter couldn't turn the crankshaft at all, but the crankshaft is turning.
A stuck piston would lock the crankshaft too, but the pistons are moving up and down smoothly.
belt_snap.cause: The timing belt has snapped. The crankshaft still turns, but the camshafts up top aren't driven, so the valves don't open and close.
belt_snap.why: Why won't the engine start with a broken timing belt, even though the crankshaft turns?
belt_snap.answer: The timing belt makes the camshafts follow the crankshaft (two crank turns, one cam turn). With the camshafts stopped, the valves don't open and close at the right time, so the cylinders can't take in fuel and air or push out exhaust, and the engine can't fire.
reasons: The timing belt drives the wheels, so with it broken the car can't move.
The timing belt powers the spark plugs, so with it broken there's no spark.
